LESSON: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.3: Trans Saharan Slave Trade
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Trans Saharan Slave Trade, part of People and Relationships in Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do people subject others to slave trade?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trans Saharan Slave Trade in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trans Saharan Slave Trade in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. outline effects of Trans- Saharan slave trade in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trans Saharan Slave Trade in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trans Saharan Slave Trade in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. desire to promote social justice in a society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trans Saharan Slave Trade in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,
2. use digital or print resources to research on the organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,
3. work together and discuss the effects of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,
4. take turns in activities and conversation as they draw a map of Africa and locate regions

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Trans Saharan Slave Trade together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: Learners use digital or print resources to research on the organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.

Values:
● Respect: Learners work together and discuss the effects of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.

● Unity: Learners take turns in activities and conversation as they draw a map of Africa and locate regions where slaves were

sourced during the Trans-Saharan slave trade.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: Learners work together amicably as they debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave

trade in Africa.

Link to other subjects:

The learner applies Creative Arts skills as they draw a map of Africa and locate regions where slaves were sourced during the

Trans-Saharan slave trade.

Main points to remember:

1. identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa,
2. describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,
3. outline effects of Trans- Saharan slave trade in Africa,
4. demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice,
5. desire to promote social justice in a society.

Remember the key question: Why do people subject others to slave trade?
